info.title: Tunploy API
info.description:
Manage devices and servers on your Tunploy VPN from your own programs, and hear about what happens to them.

Send an API key from Settings → API keys as `Authorization: Bearer tp_…`. Each key only does what its scopes allow. Requests are limited to 10 a second per key, with bursts up to 60. Keep keys on your server, never in an app.

Errors always look like `{"error": {"code": "…", "message": "…", "fields": {…}}}`; `fields` names the inputs a validation error is about.

post.description:
Send `public_key` to keep the private key on the client; the config then has no PrivateKey line. Send `server_id: "auto"` (with `country` or `city` if you like) to let the panel pick the emptiest running server.

Needs the `devices:write` scope.

post.description:
The device keeps its ID, keys, name, limits and usage history. It gets an address on the new server, and the server's endpoint and key change, so the client needs the new `config` from the reply. With `server_id: "auto"` the server it is on now is never picked.

Needs the `devices:write` scope.

Sets the fields sent on every device in the group: renew a plan with `expires_at`, or end it with `enabled: false`. Every device is checked first, so a value that is wrong for one changes none.

Needs the `devices:write` scope.

post.description:
Deploys the server before it answers, which can take a while when the image is new to the machine. A 201 is a running server; a failed deploy leaves nothing behind.

Needs the `servers:write` scope.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: A retry with the same key within 24 hours gets the first reply back (with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`) instead of running again.

node_id.description: The machine to run on, from `GET /nodes`; 0, the default, is the panel's own.

address.description: The server's address and subnet, such as `10.20.0.1/22`, between /16 and /30. Defaults to a free /24.

max_devices.description: Instead of `address`: the smallest free subnet, /24 or larger, that holds this many devices.

endpoint.description: Host clients dial, without a port. Defaults to the panel's public host, or the node's.

listen_port.description: UDP; unique per machine. Defaults to the next free one from 51820.

client_allowed_ips.description: What clients send through the tunnel; defaults to everything.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2. Guessed from the endpoint on create when left out.

patch.description:
Only the fields sent change. The address and node are fixed. A new `listen_port` or `mtu` recreates the container, which drops connections for a moment; the rest apply to configs issued from now on.

Needs the `servers:write` scope.

endpoint.description: Host clients dial, without a port. Defaults to the panel's public host, or the node's.

listen_port.description: UDP; unique per machine. Defaults to the next free one from 51820.

client_allowed_ips.description: What clients send through the tunnel; defaults to everything.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2. Guessed from the endpoint on create when left out.

409.description: `server_not_empty`: the server has devices and `force` is not `true`.

delete.description:
Removes the container and every device on it. A server that has devices needs `?force=true`, so a stale ID cannot cut off users by accident; move them with `POST /devices/{id}/move` first if they should keep working.

Needs the `servers:write` scope.

parameters.name: force
parameters.description: Delete the server's devices with it.

get.description:
The machines servers can run on. The panel's own is first, with ID 0. Nodes are added in the panel, since that takes SSH access.

Needs the `servers:read` scope.

Devices, servers and nodes only; sign-ins and settings stay in the panel. Keep the last ID you saw and ask again with `after`. Events are kept for 90 days.

Needs the `events:read` scope.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Only events with a larger ID.

200.description: All webhooks, has_more is always false.

201.description: The webhook with its signing secret, shown this once.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: A retry with the same key within 24 hours gets the first reply back (with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`) instead of running again.

url.description: http or https, without a user name or password.

enabled.description: Turning a webhook off gives up on its pending deliveries.

post.description:
Sends an event of kind `ping`, whatever the webhook subscribes to.

Needs the `webhooks:write` scope.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: Cursor: the last ID of the previous page.

post.description:
Posted to each webhook that subscribes to the event's kind. Check `X-Tunploy-Signature` before trusting the body: `t=<unix time>,v1=<hex>`, where v1 is HMAC-SHA256 over `<t>.<raw body>` keyed with the webhook's secret. Turn away timestamps more than a few minutes old.

Answer with a 2xx within 10 seconds. Anything else, a timeout or a redirect is tried again after 1 and 5 minutes, 30 minutes, 2, 6 and 12 hours, then given up. Deliveries can arrive out of order and more than once: use the event ID or X-Tunploy-Delivery to skip repeats.

BadRequest.description: `invalid_request`: a query parameter or the body could not be read.

Unauthorized.description: `unauthorized`: no key, or it is unknown, revoked or expired.

Forbidden.description: `missing_scope`: the key lacks the scope this needs.

Invalid.description: `validation_failed`: `fields` says what is wrong with which input.

Traffic.description: Seen from the server: rx is what the device uploaded, tx what it downloaded.

LimitPeriod.description: monthly counts from the first of each month in the panel's time zone; total counts until a usage reset.

external_id.description: Your own ID for the device's owner. Not unique.

address.description: The device's address inside the tunnel.

client_key.description: The client made the key pair; the panel never saw the private key.

online.description: As of the panel's last look, at most ten seconds old.

data_limit.description: Bytes per limit period, both directions; 0 means no limit.

period_usage.description: What counts toward data_limit: this month, or since the last usage reset.

usage_reset_at.description: The last usage reset, if any.

month_usage.description: The calendar month, whatever the limit period.

config.description: Only in the reply to a create: the WireGuard config. Holds the private key unless public_key was sent.

has_more.description: More items follow; ask again with the last ID as the cursor.

month_usage.description: All the devices together, this calendar month.

start.description: First day of the day or month, in the panel's time zone.

endpoint.description: Host clients dial; the port is listen_port.

address.description: The server's own address in its subnet.

capacity.description: How many devices fit; creating more fails with server_full.

has_more.description: More items follow; ask again with the last ID as the cursor.

detail.description: Human-readable extra, such as the usage when a limit is reached.

actor.description: `api:<key name>` when an API key caused it; empty for the admin or the panel itself.

has_more.description: More items follow; ask again with the last ID as the cursor.

secret.description: Signs every delivery. Shown this once.

has_more.description: More items follow; ask again with the last ID as the cursor.

id.description: Sent as X-Tunploy-Delivery; the same on every retry.

has_more.description: More items follow; ask again with the last ID as the cursor.
